w10_T4_002848: A charity race began the morning with 172 minutes of total volunteer time logged. That time was split evenly between 2 shifts, and only the morning shift's minutes were tracked. Since the race logs everything in minutes but the coordinator prefers reporting hours to sponsors, she always converted the number before sending updates. By evening, 43 more minutes were logged from a late sign-up. Overnight, 21 minutes had to be subtracted after a scheduling error was found. How many minutes were logged by the next morning?
w10_T4_002850: A charity auction began with 113 dollars pledged before the bidding started. A promotional matching pledge doubled that amount. A vendor fee, unrelated to the 300 raffle tickets printed for a separate drawing, then cost the auction 117 dollars. A final matching-donor round made the remaining total grow to 7 times its size. A processing fee removed 723 dollars before the funds were released. How much money was released to the charity?
w10_T4_002863: A furniture store started the morning with 222 chairs in the warehouse, while a dozen display chairs sat in the front window, never counted in inventory. A holiday sale required the store to restock 5 times as many chairs as remained. A final delivery added 51 more chairs. How many chairs were in the warehouse after that delivery?
w10_T4_002866: A comic book warehouse began the morning with 4 identical sections, each holding 231 comics, combined into one inventory total. By midday, 366 comics were shipped out to a distributor. w10_T4_002888: Two roommates, Isaac and Nora, tracked shared grocery funds, and Nora's contribution always trailed his. Isaac put in 57 dollars at the start of the month. w10_T4_002901: A theater sold 200 tickets by the morning box office opening. w10_T4_002902: A charity walk began with 58 dollars pledged at sign-up, while a separate fun run nearby collected 500 water bottles for its own runners, unrelated to this event. w10_T4_002912: Two neighbors, Tessa and Roman, tracked stacked firewood, and Roman's pile always fell short of hers. Tessa started with 40 logs, and a delivery doubled her pile right away. w10_T4_002916: Two shop owners, Bettina and Marcus, tracked shoe inventory, and Marcus's stock always trailed hers. w10_T4_002921: Two coworkers, Dana and Miguel, tracked commission dollars, and Miguel's total always ran behind hers. Dana's commission started the week at 181 dollars. w10_T4_002934: A furniture workshop began the week with 3 identical carpenters, each building 147 chairs, combined into one production total. A shipping delay removed 252 chairs from that total. w10_T4_002940: Two joggers, Bella and Tomas, tracked morning mileage, and Tomas always logged less than she did. w10_T4_002946: A charity car wash began the morning with 122 dollars collected. By midmorning, 71 more dollars came in. A matching pledge doubled that total. w10_T4_002950: Two clerks, Odalys and Bram, tracked register cash, and Bram's drawer always held less than hers. Odalys's drawer started the shift with 105 dollars. w10_T4_002952: Two roommates, Priya and Elias, tracked their shared snack fund, and Elias's contribution always fell behind hers. Priya put in 232 dollars at the start of the semester. w10_T4_002955: Two artists, Lucia and Faron, tracked mural paint cans, and Faron always used fewer cans than she did. w10_T4_002959: A juice stand started the morning with 128 cups sold already. By midmorning, 111 cups had to be discarded after a machine malfunction. In the afternoon, 52 more cups were sold. w10_T4_002988: A food truck began the morning with 55 dollars in the cash box.
